entities.name: Giacomo Orsini
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Giacomo Orsini (also known as Jacopo Orsini), a scion of the powerful Roman Orsini family, was a significant prelate whose career culminated as the cardinal deacon of San Giorgio in Velabro from 1371 until his death on August 21, 1379. His ecclesiastical prominence coincided with the tumultuous return of the papacy from Avignon to Rome and the immediate genesis of the Western Schism, placing him at the epicenter of one of the most profound crises in medieval Church history. As a cardinal, Orsini was deeply embedded in the intricate web of Roman politics and papal administration, wielding influence derived from both his noble lineage and his high clerical office during a period of intense factionalism.

Elevated to the cardinalate by Pope Gregory XI in 1371, Giacomo Orsini played a critical role in the two pivotal papal conclaves of 1378. He was among the cardinals who, under immense pressure from the Roman populace, elected Pope Urban VI in April 1378, marking the end of the Avignon Papacy. However, rapidly disillusioned by Urban VI's erratic behavior and perceived tyranny, Orsini subsequently joined the dissenting cardinals who, only months later in September 1378, declared Urban's election invalid and proceeded to elect Robert of Geneva as Pope Clement VII in Fondi. This second election formally initiated the Western Schism, dividing Christendom for nearly forty years.

Orsini's decision to align with Clement VII and the Avignon obedience cemented his position as a prominent figure in the schismatic papacy, contributing to the deep divisions within the College of Cardinals and the broader Church. His death, occurring just over a year after the dual elections, meant he did not witness the full, protracted consequences of the schism he helped inaugurate. Nevertheless, his actions underscored the deep political and personal rifts that plagued the late medieval Church, transforming a crisis of papal authority into a sustained institutional rupture.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Giacomo Orsini's direct participation in both papal conclaves of 1378, particularly his role in the election of Clement VII, was instrumental in the immediate outbreak of the Western Schism, fracturing the Catholic Church for decades. His actions directly contributed to one of the most significant institutional crises of the medieval period.
